chunks: And Hammad narrated from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said:
I asked him about the saying of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic:
“Then appoint an arbitrator from his family and an arbitrator from her family.”

He عليه السلام said: “The two arbitrators do not have the right to separate until they seek the permission of the man and the woman, and stipulate upon them that if they wish they reconcile them, and if they wish they separate them. So if they reconcile them, it is valid, and if they separate them, it is valid.”

key_terms.أَهْلِهَا: her family, from whom one arbitrator is appointed
key_terms.أَهْلِهِ: his family, from whom one arbitrator is appointed
key_terms.الْحَكَمَيْنِ: the two appointed arbiters in the marital dispute
key_terms.جَمَعَا: they reconciled and brought the spouses together
key_terms.حَكَمًا: an arbitrator appointed to judge or mediate between spouses
key_terms.يَسْتَأْمِرَا: to seek the instruction or permission of the spouses

ai.seo_question: What authority do the two family arbitrators have in resolving marital discord according to Qur'an 4:35?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the verse about appointing arbiters in cases of marital discord. It clarifies that the two arbiters act after consulting the husband and wife and establishing agreed authority, and that either reconciliation or separation, once carried out under those terms, is valid.
